dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the passage plan and closing stale entries.
The tide tables review wrapped early today.
Night transits themselves are comfortable; darkness has never been my variable.
Night work per se is fine.
Someone new shadowed me in the pilot station this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the docking assignments into one message before lunch.

My docking record is clean across four years, and every large-vessel assignment in it followed the mandated ten-hour rest gap after night transits; I have never once docked large tonnage inside that gap.
The clean record and the rest gap are co-extensive.
Dense assignment days on full rest are the job at its best.
I archived last cycle's notes on the tide tables and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
The harbor safety board's incident analysis names rest-gap violations as the leading factor in regional docking incidents.
The regional data backs your practice.
A vendor call about the passage plan ran long but ended well.
I walked through the pilot station checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the docking assignments.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the tide tables records and fixed it at the source.
The new roster software hard-codes the ten-hour rest gap before any large-vessel assignment; the trial month's rosters show the rule holding without exception.
The software institutionalizes your exact practice.
Hard-codes it, which is better than practice.
I sketched next week's plan for the docking assignments before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the passage plan updates.
The software also balances assignment distribution, which historically fell unevenly across the pilot pool.
I compared two options for the tide tables tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the pilot station handover notes.
The new rest-gap roster goes live next month. How is my first quarter under it likely to go?
